import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 973

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
- [Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of
  complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
-/

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos973

/--
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
          z 1 = 1 ∧
          (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧
          (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.le_one :
    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∀ M_2 : ℝ,
      IsGLB { M | ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        (∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∃ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧
        (∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), M = ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧
          ∀ m ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M) } M_2 →
      (1.746 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < (1.745 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.tang :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥
        (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos973

findings.description: The leading `∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 →` turns an estimate for sufficiently large n into an estimate for every n ≥ 2. The upper bound is false at n = 2. For any admissible pair, relabel a unit-modulus entry as a and the other as b. The identity `2*a^4 = (a^2-a*b-b^2)*(a^2+b^2) + (a+b)*(a^3+b^3)` and the triangle inequality give `2 ≤ 5 * max (‖a^2+b^2‖) (‖a^3+b^3‖)`. Consequently the actual GLB is at least 2/5, whereas `1.745^(-2) < 2/5`. The GLB hypothesis is satisfiable, not vacuous. `/workspace/review/counterexample.lean` contains a sorry-free refutation of the stated all-n bound; its axiom dependencies do not include `sorryAx`.
findings.source_evidence: L. Erdős, “On some problems of P. Turán concerning power sums of complex numbers,” Acta Math. Hung. 59 (1992), p.12: Theorem 1 gives the estimates “for sufficiently large n,” and the numerical-bound Corollary explicitly begins “For n > n₀.” Primary scan: https://real-j.mtak.hu/7456/1/MTA_ActaMathHung_59.pdf (PDF p.18). Quanyu Tang’s comment at 16:01 on 10 October 2025 likewise states `(1.746)^(-n) < M₂ < (1.745)^(-n)` for `n > n₀`: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/973. The main page’s abbreviated summary omits this qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∀ M_2 : ℝ, ...` with `∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ M_2 : ℝ, ...`, retaining the existing IsGLB predicate and inequalities. Add “for sufficiently large n” to the docstring. Keep the solved category.

reformulations.difference: The extremum encoding itself—not the erroneous n-range—uses `∀ M_2, IsGLB {attained maxima} M_2 → ...` instead of explicitly defining M₂ as a minimum over finite complex tuples.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 2, the admissible finite tuples form a nonempty compact set: the closed unit polydisk intersected with the condition that at least one coordinate has modulus 1. The finite maximum of the power-sum moduli is continuous, so its image is nonempty and compact and has an attained, unique infimum. Thus the IsGLB determines exactly the source’s minimum. Functions ℕ → ℂ merely extend the finite tuple outside the indices used. The existential maximizing k and the normalization conjunction are equivalent to the corresponding finite maxima; those equivalences and GLB existence were checked in Lean. Compactness and attainment are justified mathematically and explicitly noted on p.11 of the primary paper.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations. The other three agree with the intended source claims. The source still labels the main question OPEN; its July 2026 proof claim is expressly unverified, so it does not justify a status change. Lean checks are in /workspace/review/{counterexample,equivalences,boundaries}.lean, with a detailed checklist in /workspace/review/checklist.md. The target file remains identical to the committed file. The original 1974 Hayman chapter and 1984 Turán book were not directly available: Hayman was cross-checked against the later arXiv edition and Erdős’s original 1965 statement; Turán’s results were checked through the quotations in Erdős 1992 and Tang’s source comments. The Hayman–Lingham draft has an apparent ≤ typo in its open-question clause, resolved by the original Erdős source and current problem page.

submission.summary: Changed m2_bounds to assert the inequalities for sufficiently large n using ∀ᶠ n in atTop, and updated its docstring accordingly. Preserved the IsGLB predicate, numerical bounds, and attributes; no other declarations were changed. The required compile command succeeded with only declaration-uses-sorry warnings.
